lab_title: Structural Anatomy and Blood Flow of the Human Heart
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers, four valves, and major blood vessels of the human heart.
Distinguish between the anatomical structures of the right and left sides of the heart, including myocardial thickness.
Trace the chronological pathway of blood through both the pulmonary and systemic circulatory loops.
Explain how the cardiac valves function to ensure unidirectional blood flow and prevent regurgitation.

scenes.brief_purpose: Orient students to the heart's location in the mediastinum and identify the major external landmarks and vessels.
key_visuals: A life-sized, translucent 3D human torso showing the thoracic cavity.
A beating 3D heart model positioned in the mediastinum.
Color-coded major vessels: blue for the Superior/Inferior Vena Cava and Pulmonary Trunk; red for the Aorta and Pulmonary Veins.
student_actions: Rotate and scale the virtual heart to inspect it from anterior, posterior, and lateral views.
Tap and label the major vessels (Aorta, Vena Cavae, Pulmonary Trunk, and Pulmonary Veins) as they enter and exit the heart.
Toggle the transparency of the thoracic cage to understand anatomical positioning.

scenes.brief_purpose: Examine the internal structure of the heart by looking at a cross-section of the four chambers.
key_visuals: A coronal cross-section of the beating heart, exposing the internal spaces.
Glowing visual highlights for each chamber: Right Atrium, Right Ventricle, Left Atrium, and Left Ventricle.
Interatrial and interventricular septa clearly visible.
student_actions: Tap each of the four chambers to reveal their names, structural characteristics (like pectinate muscles and trabeculae carneae), and basic functions.
Place label pins into the correct chamber based on clinical prompts (e.g., "Identify the chamber that receives deoxygenated blood from the systemic circuit").

scenes.brief_purpose: Identify the four heart valves, classify them, and observe how they prevent the backflow of blood during the cardiac cycle.
key_visuals: Close-up, top-down view of the fibrous skeleton of the heart showing all four valves (Tricuspid, Mitral/Bicuspid, Pulmonary, Aortic) opening and closing.
Sub-structures like chordae tendineae and papillary muscles holding the AV valves.
Dynamic arrows showing blood flowing forward through open valves and stopping at closed valves.
student_actions: Use an interactive time-scrubber to slow down the heartbeat, observing when the AV valves open/close relative to the semilunar valves.
Sort the four valves into their respective categories: Atrioventricular (AV) vs. Semilunar (SL).
Induce a simulated "valve prolapse" via a toggle to visualize how damaged chordae tendineae lead to backflow (regurgitation) into the atrium.

scenes.brief_purpose: Compare the muscular thickness of the left and right ventricular walls and correlate this structural difference with their physiological workloads.
key_visuals: A transverse (cross-sectional) slice through both the left and right ventricles.
Clear visual contrast between the thin, crescent-shaped wall of the Right Ventricle and the thick, circular wall of the Left Ventricle.
A schematic pressure gauge displaying the resistance of the pulmonary circuit (low pressure) versus the systemic circuit (high pressure).
student_actions: Use a virtual caliper tool to measure and compare the thickness (in millimeters) of the left ventricular myocardium versus the right ventricular myocardium.
Select the correct physiological explanation from a multiple-choice panel relating wall thickness to the systemic systemic vascular resistance that the left ventricle must overcome.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the pathway of deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary circuit (right side of the heart to the lungs).
key_visuals: A glowing, blue pathway of deoxygenated blood flowing through the right side of the heart.
Close-up views of the Tricuspid valve opening to let blood into the Right Ventricle, and the Pulmonary valve opening to push blood into the Pulmonary Trunk.
Two simplified lungs on either side of the heart showing where the pulmonary arteries terminate.
student_actions: Physically walk around the AR model to trace the flow of a virtual "deoxygenated blood cell" (blue sphere) from the Vena Cava to the Pulmonary Arteries.
Drag and drop anatomical landmarks (Right Atrium, Tricuspid Valve, Right Ventricle, Pulmonary Valve) into the correct sequential order to complete the pathway.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the pathway of oxygenated blood through the systemic circuit (left side of the heart to the rest of the body).
key_visuals: A glowing, red pathway of oxygenated blood returning from the lungs and entering the left side of the heart.
Close-up views of the Mitral/Bicuspid valve opening into the Left Ventricle, and the Aortic valve opening to push blood into the Aorta.
A simplified systemic capillary bed representing the upper and lower body receiving the oxygenated blood.
student_actions: Trace the flow of an "oxygenated blood cell" (red sphere) starting from the Pulmonary Veins, through the Left Atrium and Ventricle, and out through the Aorta.
Drag and drop the left-side anatomical structures (Pulmonary Veins, Left Atrium, Mitral Valve, Left Ventricle, Aortic Valve, Aorta) into the correct sequential order.

scenes.brief_purpose: Synthesize knowledge of the complete cardiac cycle and dual-loop circulation through an interactive pathfinding assessment.
key_visuals: The complete, beating heart with both blue and red pathways running simultaneously (dual-loop circulation).
A blank sequential board on one side of the workspace.
student_actions: Arrange a scrambled list of 10 anatomical structures into the precise chronological order that blood travels, starting from the systemic veins and ending at the systemic arteries.
Trigger a "real-time flow test" where a virtual blood cell flows through the 3D heart following the student's customized sequence, visually highlighting any routing errors they made.
